title: Aggrega Plugin Trust Record
description: Machine-generated record of the plugin identity trusted for each attachment that returns an accept-or-reject verdict — a `plugins.governance` attachment in an `ir-verdict` or `render-verdict` role, and every `plugins.linter` attachment. Lives at `plugins-trust.yaml` beside the lockfile and is committed alongside it, because a record held outside version control is one nobody can review and nothing can compare against. Written by `aggrega pull`, which creates the file the first time it resolves one of those attachments and adds a record per attachment as it resolves it. A file carrying records for only some of the configured attachments is a valid intermediate state rather than a damaged one. Read by `aggrega build`, by `aggrega lint --release` and by `aggrega validate --release`, and by the same operations reached through `aggrega serve` and `aggrega mcp`; each holds the workspace configuration to the record before any of those attachments runs. Two disagreements are refused, for different reasons: a plugin whose resolved artifact digest is not the digest recorded for it is refused rather than run, because the plugin that would run is not the one the record was reviewed for; and a record entry that no configured verdict attachment accounts for halts the run, because dropping a gate changes no rendered byte, so output produced without a gate that was reviewed is indistinguishable from output that gate approved. The opposite direction — a configured attachment the record does not yet hold — is the intermediate state just described and refuses nothing, and an absent record holds no entries at all, so it pins nothing and refuses nothing. An entry leaves the record only on an explicit upgrade: `aggrega pull --upgrade` naming a plugin drops that plugin's entry when no verdict attachment names it any more, and a bare `aggrega pull --upgrade` drops every such entry. A plain `aggrega pull` neither rewrites nor removes an entry, so a halt over an entry nothing accounts for is cleared by saying so deliberately rather than by the next run. A record whose last entry is dropped is emptied rather than deleted, and an emptied record is a valid one: it holds nothing, so it pins nothing and refuses nothing, exactly as an absent record does. Each record is addressed by the plugin's own identity coordinate and carries the selected version and the artifact digest as fields, so a version change is a change to a field of an existing record rather than a new record under a new address — which is what makes a re-versioned plugin distinguishable, in the file and in its diff, from one recorded for the first time. This file records identity and nothing else: no signature, no rule inputs, and no resolution provenance — no registry host, no path on the machine that wrote it — so the same resolution produces the same bytes wherever it runs. A `plugins.governance` verdict attachment's external rule files are recorded as digests in the lockfile's `verdict_inputs`; a `plugins.linter` attachment's rule inputs are recorded in neither file. Everything a build reproduces byte-for-byte is pinned in the lockfile instead; a verdict attachment shapes none of the rendered output, which is why its identity is recorded here rather than there. Schema evolution discipline: adding a new top-level section is SemVer-MINOR (additive); adding a new field inside an existing section is SemVer-MINOR; removing a key or tightening a constraint is SemVer-MAJOR.

plugins.description: One record per plugin trusted for a verdict-returning attachment, addressed by the plugin's identity coordinate. A plugin attached at two verdict roles at once — the same governance plugin bound to both `ir-verdict` and `render-verdict` — contributes a single record, because the recorded subject is the plugin's identity rather than the attachment: the two attachments read the same artifact. Records are emitted in ascending coordinate order.

plugin.description: The plugin's identity coordinate: its socket segment and its bare name joined by a slash, as in `governance/aggrega-security-baseline`. A bare name is unique only within its socket, so the socket segment is what distinguishes two same-named plugins in different sockets. The coordinate deliberately carries no version — that is what makes a version change visible as an edit to `resolved_version` below rather than as an unrelated record.

resolved_version.description: Concrete version selected for this plugin when the record was written (e.g. `1.2.3`).

digest.description: Content digest of the resolved plugin artifact (e.g. `sha256:...`).

version.description: Trust-record schema version. Currently 1; future SemVer-MAJOR breaks of the schema increment this integer.
